title: Add jurisdictional KMS consent bridge and configurable audit redaction policy
author: Ayesha Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces a lightweight 'kms-consent-bridge' middleware and a configurable audit redaction layer to enforce jurisdictional KMS consent and remove PII from audit payloads for regulated tenants. Motivation: customers operating across jurisdictions requested a deterministic way to ensure KMS calls honor tenant residency constraints while preserving minimal, queryable audit telemetry. This PR implements the consent handshake, residency check cache, RBAC v2 operator-scope binding to limit who can bypass consent, and a redaction policy engine that runs before audit emission.

What changed (high level commits):
- feat: add kms-consent-bridge service and gRPC API (handles consent handshake, evidence caching, primary/secondary KMS selection)
- feat: residency-checker library with pluggable backends (cloud metadata, static config, remote attestor)
- feat: audit-redactor engine (yaml policy driven) and default PII rule set
- refactor: routing middleware to call consent-bridge in pre-invoke hook; added timeout and fallback path for legacy mode
- docs: operator guide and compliance playbook with examples for EU, APAC deployments
- test: unit + e2e harness updates including simulated multi-region KMS path and audit sink assertions

Files touched (representative):
- services/kms-consent-bridge/main.go
- services/kms-consent-bridge/consent/handshake.go
- libs/residency-checker/residency.go
- runtime/middleware/kms_consent_middleware.go
- runtime/audit/redactor/redactor.go
- infra/helm/kms-consent-bridge/values.yaml
- docs/ops/jurisdictional-kms.md
- tests/e2e/consent_bridge_multi_region_test.go
- examples/operator/policies/example-redaction.yaml

Design notes:
- Consent handshake is optimistic with a short TTL cache (30s by default) and proof-of-decision record emitted as 'consent.proof' in audit metadata; customers can configure longer caching per deployment.
- Fallback behavior: if consent-bridge is unreachable, middleware enforces a tenant-configurable fail-mode: 'deny' (default for strict deployments) or 'allow-with-warning' for permissive/dev environments.
- RBAC v2 changes: introduced a new operator scope claim 'rbac:region-bypass' that must be granted explicitly via policy templates; bypass audit logs are annotated and cannot be redacted by tenant-level redaction rules.
- Audit redaction engine: policy authored in YAML supports 'remove', 'mask', and 'hash' actions per JSONPath. Default rules target common PII keys but customers can supply their own policy via the console or helm.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added and passing locally; [x] e2e harness updated with multi-region scenario; [x] Helm chart and infra config added; [x] Docs and runbook updated; [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_jurisdictional_kms` for staged rollout.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Marta Novak (reviewer): "Can we avoid blocking all requests if the bridge is NACKing transiently? Suggest exponential backoff and soft-fail mode for initial rollout."
- Author (Ayesha): "Added backoff + a `fail_mode` flag exposed via helm; default remains 'deny' for strict compliance customers. Documented tradeoffs in ops runbook."
- Diego Rivera (security): "Ensure redaction policy cannot be overridden by tenant to remove operator bypass traces."
- Author: "Implemented policy scoping: cluster-level 'protected' rules are applied after tenant rules and cannot be removed unless operator has `rbac:override-audit-policy` role; tests updated."
- Priya Singh (infra): "Helm values look fine but add readiness probe and resource requests for the bridge."
- Author: "Added readiness/liveness and conservative resource defaults; noted scaling guidance in docs."

CI summary: initial CI run: build passed, unit tests failed (flaky residency-checker race) -> fixed by syncing the TTL and adding locking; rerun succeeded. Integration suite: one flaky e2e failure in private-installer that required bumping Helm chart dependencies; final run green. Checks: build (pass), unit (pass), e2e (pass), lint (pass), security-scan (pass).

Impact and rollout: Feature flagged and will be rolled out to a small subset of customers on Dedicated and Private first; Hosted customers will see console toggle. No data migration required. Operational concerns captured in docs (ops/jurisdictional-kms.md) including runbook for 'consent-bridge' downtime.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main. Release notes included below.
release_notes: Added jurisdictional KMS consent bridge (feature-flagged) and a configurable audit redaction engine. Operators can enforce tenant residency constraints and protect audit traces. Rolled out behind `enable_jurisdictional_kms`. See docs/ops/jurisdictional-kms.md for migration and runbook.
notes: This PR implements a compliance-focused path: customers with strict residency needs should enable `fail_mode: deny` in their helm values. For gradual rollout, use 'allow-with-warning' and monitor `consent.bridge.failures` and `audit.redactor.drops` metrics.
